rationale: Hebrews 11:8-12 names Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Sarah, and 11:13 goes on: 'All these people died in faith, without having received the things they were promised. However, they saw them and welcomed them from afar' (BSB). Genesis narrates Abraham's death only at 25:7-8. Several commentators on Hebrews 11:13 limit 'All these' to the patriarchs: Barnes, Meyer and the Expositor's Greek Testament name Abraham, Sarah, Isaac and Jacob, and the Pulpit Commentary names Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. On their reading the verse refers to the death this lesson's passage narrates. Two named readers of Genesis 25:8 read it beside Hebrews 11:13: Keil (the phrase 'gathered to his people' rests on a hope 'which the promises of God had exalted in the case of the patriarchs into a firm assurance of faith (Hebrews 11:13)'), and the Pulpit Commentary ('Abraham died in the hope of a better country, even an heavenly (Hebrews 11:13-16)'). Graded explicit_reference, following conn-gen12-call-hebrews11-8, because Hebrews names Abraham and speaks of his death without quoting Genesis. Graded strong rather than explicit, following conn-gen18-sarah-faith-hebrews11, for two reasons. First, Hebrews names no Genesis scene and quotes none of 25:8's words. Second, the scope of 'All these' is disputed: Jamieson-Fausset-Brown say the 'ALL' 'can hardly but include Abel, Enoch, and Noah', and Meyer reports Oecumenius, Theophylact and others taking it of everyone named from Abel on except Enoch. On either reading Abraham is included. The row claims only that Hebrews refers to Abraham's death; what Hebrews says about the hope behind it is the author's statement, and the lesson reports readings of 25:8 on the afterlife without deciding between them.
